industries.name: Financial Services & Banking
industries.archetype: High regulatory exposure, system-critical, zero tolerance for downtime

scenarios.name: Core Banking System Failure
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: RM 800K–1.2M per hour in lost transaction fees and operational costs
scenarios.trigger_text: A critical software patch deployed overnight causes the core banking platform to crash at 7:00 AM on a Monday morning. Tellers are frozen at their terminals. The phones are ringing.
scenarios.threat_summary: System outage caused by a failed software patch — total core banking platform failure during peak hours.

escalation_waves.event: ATMs nationwide go offline. Branch tellers cannot process any transactions. Customer calls are flooding the contact centre — hold times exceed 45 minutes.
#BankDown is trending on social media. Journalists are calling Corporate Communications for a statement. Customer anger is escalating publicly.
The Central Bank must now be formally notified. The regulatory breach clock has started. The CEO has been pulled from a board meeting.
Estimated revenue loss reaches RM 4.2M. Institutional clients are escalating to their relationship managers and threatening to move funds.
National media coverage. A competitor quietly issues a press release highlighting their uptime record. Staff morale is visibly affected.
Regulator issues a formal request for a full incident report within 5 business days. Legal counsel is now involved.

recovery_levers.label: Activate Backup Systems
recovery_levers.description: Switch to your disaster recovery site and restore core banking systems from last clean backup.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Backup activation fails — IT team not available to execute the failover.

recovery_levers.label: Manual Operations Mode
recovery_levers.description: Deploy manual transaction processing at priority branches while systems recover.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No one is available to coordinate branch manual procedures.

recovery_levers.label: Issue Public Statement
recovery_levers.description: Release a holding statement to media and customers acknowledging the issue and estimated resolution time.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No authorised spokesperson — unofficial statements leak and worsen the situation.

recovery_levers.label: Proactively Notify Regulator
recovery_levers.description: Contact the Central Bank before the mandatory deadline — demonstrate transparency and good faith.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Notification missed or delayed — regulator finds out from media instead.

recovery_levers.label: Customer Compensation Protocol
recovery_levers.description: Activate fee waivers and goodwill credits for affected customers to protect loyalty.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Compensation cannot be processed — customer anger compounds.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lesson: IT recovery speed is critical but the regulatory clock runs independently. Teams often forget Compliance until it is too late. The dependency between IT and Operations for manual fallback is frequently underestimated.

scenarios.name: Targeted Ransomware Attack
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: USD 2M ransom demand + RM 3–8M estimated remediation and legal costs
scenarios.trigger_text: At 11:30 PM, the IT security team detects encrypted files spreading rapidly across internal servers. A ransom note appears on every compromised screen: USD 2,000,000 in cryptocurrency. 48 hours. Or the data goes public.
scenarios.threat_summary: Ransomware attack with data breach — customer records compromised, 48-hour ransom deadline.

escalation_waves.event: IT has isolated affected servers but 40% of internal systems are already compromised. The attack is still spreading through unpatched segments.
Customer data breach confirmed. PDPA obligations are triggered immediately — notification deadline clock has started.
Board convened for emergency session. Insurers have been notified. The ransom deadline is now 40 hours away.
An anonymous source has leaked the story to media. Stock price drops 6% at market opening. Customers begin withdrawing funds.
Regulator launches a formal investigation. An external forensic firm has been engaged. Legal costs are escalating rapidly.
Full scope of breach confirmed: 280,000 customer records compromised. Class action lawsuit filed.

recovery_levers.label: Engage Cybersecurity Response Team
recovery_levers.description: Bring in an external cybersecurity incident response firm to contain and eradicate the attack. Do NOT pay the ransom.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No internal capability to brief the response firm — containment delayed by 12 hours.

recovery_levers.label: Restore from Clean Backup
recovery_levers.description: Identify and restore systems from the last verified clean backup. Validate backup integrity before execution.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Backup restoration cannot proceed without IT team oversight.

recovery_levers.label: Notify Affected Customers
recovery_levers.description: Proactively notify all 280,000 affected customers within 72 hours as required by PDPA. Include what data was exposed and what they should do.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Notification is legally required — failure to notify adds regulatory penalties.

recovery_levers.label: Crisis Communications Response
recovery_levers.description: Issue a transparent public statement. Hold a press briefing. Emphasise swift action and customer protection steps taken.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No authorised spokesperson — silence interpreted as concealment by media.

recovery_levers.label: Proactive Regulator Engagement
recovery_levers.description: Brief the regulator with a remediation roadmap before they formally investigate. Demonstrate accountability.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Regulator receives no proactive briefing — investigation scope widens.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lesson: Paying the ransom is never listed as a lever — this should provoke discussion. Teams often spend heavily on IT recovery but neglect the PDPA customer notification obligation, which has a hard legal deadline independent of technical recovery. The media leak wave surprises teams who thought containment was complete.

industries.name: Logistics & Transportation — Highway Concessionaire
industries.archetype: Physical infrastructure-dependent, public safety obligation, government concession agreement

scenarios.name: Flash Flood — Partial Highway Closure
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: RM 200K–800K in lost toll revenue per day depending on closure scope
scenarios.trigger_text: Overnight monsoon rainfall has caused flash flooding at three low-lying interchange sections. Traffic sensors trigger automatic alerts at 5:15 AM. The morning commute is already building. Three interchanges are impassable.
scenarios.threat_summary: Seasonal flash flood causing partial highway closure during peak commute hours — public safety and concession SLA obligations triggered.

escalation_waves.event: Three interchanges are closed. Traffic backs up 12 kilometres. Commuter social media posts are going viral — frustrated drivers are filming and posting in real time.
Media helicopters are overhead. Press calls are flooding the Corporate Communications line. A radio station has put an angry commuter on air.
A vehicle is reported stranded in rising floodwater at Interchange 2. Emergency services have been called. The liability clock has started.
JKR and JPJ have arrived on site. Your concession agreement response time SLA is now under review. Penalty clause exposure is being assessed.
Total toll revenue loss reaches RM 620K. Both alternative diversion routes are now at gridlock capacity.
The Ministry of Works has formally requested an incident report. An opposition politician has made a public statement about poor infrastructure maintenance.

recovery_levers.label: Deploy Flood Response Team
recovery_levers.description: Activate flood SOP: deploy water pumps, road closure barriers, and diversion signage at all three interchanges immediately.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Flood response equipment sits in depot — no team authorised to deploy without Operations.

recovery_levers.label: Real-Time Public Traffic Updates
recovery_levers.description: Push live updates to Waze, radio traffic services, and official social media. Tell commuters exactly what is closed and what is open.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No updates reach commuters — frustration compounds and media narrative worsens.

recovery_levers.label: Emergency Response to Stranded Vehicle
recovery_levers.description: Dispatch emergency response unit to the stranded vehicle at Interchange 2 immediately — this is the top safety priority.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Incident response team unavailable — emergency services arrive without concessionaire support, increasing liability.

recovery_levers.label: Notify Concession Authority
recovery_levers.description: Proactively notify JKR, JPJ, and Ministry of Works within 2 hours — before they arrive on site uninvited.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Authorities arrive on site with no prior briefing — relationship and penalty exposure worsens.

recovery_levers.label: Structural Integrity Inspection
recovery_levers.description: Engage structural engineers for a rapid post-flood inspection protocol. Required before reopening — demonstrates responsibility.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Road reopened without inspection — creates future liability if further incidents occur.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lesson: Highway concessionaires have layered obligations — public safety first, then regulatory (concession SLA), then reputation. Teams frequently prioritise media response over the stranded vehicle, which is a governance failure. The JKR/JPJ SLA wave surprises teams who assumed flooding is a force majeure exemption.

scenarios.name: Multi-Vehicle Accident — Major Expressway Closure
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: Potential RM 5–15M in liability, regulatory penalties, and reputational costs
scenarios.trigger_text: A 14-vehicle pile-up involving two tanker lorries occurs at 7:30 AM on the northbound carriageway. Full closure activated. One tanker is on its side. Fuel is leaking onto the road surface. Emergency services are en route.
scenarios.threat_summary: Major traffic accident with fuel spill, fatalities, and full carriageway closure during peak hour — multi-agency response, media, and legal liability.

escalation_waves.event: Full northbound closure is active. EMRS, BOMBA, and POLIS DIRAJA have been called. Hazmat protocol initiated for the fuel spill. 8 km of traffic backed up.
Three fatalities confirmed. Next-of-kin notification process begins. Media vehicles have arrived. Camera crews are filming from the overhead bridge.
Fuel spill confirmed as environmentally hazardous. Department of Environment (DOE) formally notified. Containment boom deployment required.
Live TV coverage on two national channels. Corporate Communications is being pressed for a press conference. Every minute of silence is being noted.
CEO issues formal public statement. Legal counsel has been engaged. Families of fatalities are being contacted by lawyers.
SPAD and Ministry of Transport have launched a formal incident investigation. Concession agreement penalty clause review is underway.

recovery_levers.label: Activate Major Incident SOP
recovery_levers.description: Establish a clear incident command structure immediately. Designate ONE authorised spokesperson. Brief all staff on communication protocol.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No command structure — multiple staff speaking to media with conflicting information.

recovery_levers.label: Issue Authorised Public Statement
recovery_levers.description: Release one authorised public statement within 60 minutes of the incident. Acknowledge, express concern, confirm agencies responding. No speculation.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Silence is interpreted as negligence. Media narrative fills the vacuum negatively.

recovery_levers.label: Fuel Spill Containment
recovery_levers.description: Coordinate with BOMBA for hazmat response and deploy containment booms. Notify DOE proactively before they arrive on site.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Spill containment delayed — DOE finds environmental damage uncontrolled, penalties increase significantly.

recovery_levers.label: Diversion Route Management
recovery_levers.description: Deploy mobile traffic management team to manage all active diversion routes. Coordinate with POLIS DIRAJA for traffic control support.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Diversion routes are unmanaged — secondary gridlock forms and media reports compound congestion.

recovery_levers.label: Preserve Evidence for Investigation
recovery_levers.description: Immediately preserve all CCTV footage, incident logs, tolling data, and maintenance records. Brief legal counsel before any regulatory interviews.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Evidence chain compromised — investigation scope widens and liability exposure increases.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lesson: This scenario tests whether teams understand the hierarchy of obligations — safety and legal evidence preservation must happen simultaneously with public communications. Teams frequently hold off the public statement waiting for 'full information' — which causes the reputation penalty to compound. The DOE environmental wave is consistently underestimated.

scenarios.name: Monsoon Landslide — Total Highway Destruction (100m Section)
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: RM 50M–200M+ in infrastructure reconstruction, regulatory penalties, revenue loss, and legal liability over 6–18 month recovery horizon
scenarios.trigger_text: At 3:20 AM during peak monsoon season, a massive landslide tears through a hillside embankment and completely destroys approximately 100 metres of your highway. All four lanes — northbound and southbound — have been swept off the alignment. Underground utilities, drainage infrastructure, fibre optic cables, and tolling conduits are gone. There is no road. The section simply does not exist anymore.
scenarios.threat_summary: Catastrophic landslide destroys 100m of full-width highway during monsoon season — total route severance, underground infrastructure loss, extended reconstruction, multi-ministry crisis.

escalation_waves.event: Emergency sensors and a patrol team confirm total route severance — all four lanes gone. No vehicles are trapped in the slide zone. Northbound and southbound traffic is backing up in both directions with no diversion in place yet. Power to the entire section and adjacent toll plazas is lost.

Morning commuters and logistics trucks are now trapped in standstills stretching 25 kilometres in both directions. Social media is in full flood — aerial drone footage of the destruction has gone viral nationally. News channels are cutting to live coverage.

JKR, IKRAM (Institute of Infrastructure Engineering), and the Slope Engineering Branch (Cawangan Kejuruteraan Cerun, JKR) have been mobilised. Geotechnical engineers confirm the slope above the destroyed section is still unstable — secondary slide risk is active. The site is a restricted zone.

The Prime Minister's office has been briefed. Ministry of Works calls an emergency press conference. Your CEO is being summoned to Putrajaya. Concession agreement force majeure clause is being reviewed — but your last slope maintenance and monitoring report is under scrutiny.

Preliminary engineering assessment confirms: minimum 6 months to reconstruct the 100m section. Underground utilities — TNB, Telekom, tolling fibre, and drainage — require independent restoration timelines. An alternate route via a federal road adds 45 minutes to the journey. Logistics companies are invoicing for consequential losses.

Parliamentary question filed demanding the Ministry explain how slope monitoring was managed under the concession. Your slope inspection maintenance records are formally requested. Opposition members allege the landslide was preventable. A class action is being organised by affected logistics operators.

Reconstruction tender awarded. Temporary Bailey bridge solution rejected by JKR due to span and load constraints. Full reconstruction cost estimate: RM 85M. Insurance claim submitted but insurer disputes whether slope maintenance obligations were met. Revenue loss now RM 14M and rising.

Geotechnical remediation of the unstable slope above the destroyed section is completed. Reconstruction enters active phase. However, a second slope 300 metres north has been flagged by IKRAM as requiring immediate monitoring — raising questions about the entire corridor's slope risk assessment.

recovery_levers.label: Activate Emergency Traffic Diversion Plan
recovery_levers.description: Immediately coordinate with JPJ and POLIS DIRAJA to activate the pre-planned diversion route via federal roads. Deploy traffic marshals at all diversion entry points.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No diversion coordination — both directions remain gridlocked for hours. Public anger compounds.

recovery_levers.label: Crisis Communications — National Level
recovery_levers.description: Brief the CEO for media. Issue a formal statement to national media within 2 hours. Engage a crisis PR firm. Establish a single authorised spokesperson. Proactively brief the Ministry before the press conference — do not let them find out from news.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No authorised spokesperson — Ministry hears about the slide from live TV. CEO is blindsided at Putrajaya.

recovery_levers.label: Mobilise Geotechnical Emergency Assessment
recovery_levers.description: Engage IKRAM and a qualified geotechnical firm within 4 hours to assess secondary slide risk and define safe exclusion zone. Required before any reconstruction work can begin.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Site declared unsafe by JKR without a geotechnical report — all recovery work halted indefinitely.

recovery_levers.label: Produce and Submit Slope Maintenance Records
recovery_levers.description: Immediately compile all slope monitoring logs, inspection records, and maintenance reports for the destroyed section. Submit proactively to JKR and the concession authority before they are formally requested.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Records cannot be located or are incomplete — regulatory investigation escalates, force majeure defence collapses.

recovery_levers.label: Underground Utilities Coordination Team
recovery_levers.description: Establish a joint coordination team with TNB, Telekom, and other utilities providers for parallel restoration planning. Separating this from road reconstruction prevents a sequential bottleneck.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Utilities restoration is uncoordinated — each provider works sequentially, extending the closure by months.

recovery_levers.label: Engage Insurance and Legal Counsel Immediately
recovery_levers.description: Notify your business interruption insurer and appoint legal counsel on Day 1. Begin building the force majeure case with contemporaneous documentation. Do not wait for the full damage assessment.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Insurance claim filed late without proper documentation — insurer disputes liability. Legal position weakened.

recovery_levers.label: Full Corridor Slope Risk Audit
recovery_levers.description: Commission an independent slope risk audit of the entire highway corridor — not just the failed section. Proactively address JKR and Parliamentary concerns before they become enforcement actions.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Second slope flagged by IKRAM catches the company unprepared — Parliamentary scrutiny intensifies.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lessons: (1) This is a Category 4 catastrophic event — the concession agreement's force majeure clause becomes central, but only if slope maintenance records are intact. Teams who did not activate LOG03-L4 early face regulatory collapse regardless of their other actions. (2) The underground utilities coordination lever is consistently overlooked — teams focus on road reconstruction and are shocked to learn utilities timelines can independently extend the closure. (3) The full corridor slope audit wave in Month 3 teaches that BCM is not just about the immediate incident — it is about demonstrating systemic safety management. (4) War chest depletion is inevitable in this scenario — the learning is in how teams prioritise their spend across safety, legal, regulatory, and reputational needs simultaneously.

scenarios.name: Flyover Section Collapse
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: RM 100M–500M+ in liability, reconstruction, legal costs, and long-term reputational damage — concession agreement termination risk
scenarios.trigger_text: At 6:45 AM, during the height of the morning rush hour, a 60-metre section of an elevated flyover on your highway collapses. Vehicles are on the flyover when it falls. Emergency services are being called from across the city. This is now a mass casualty incident.
scenarios.threat_summary: Catastrophic structural collapse of a flyover section during peak hours — mass casualty event, criminal liability exposure, potential concession termination, and national infrastructure confidence crisis.

escalation_waves.event: Confirmed: multiple vehicles have fallen with the structure. Search and rescue is underway. EMRS, BOMBA, and POLIS DIRAJA are on site. The entire highway is closed in both directions. The structural integrity of adjacent flyover sections is unknown. The nation is watching.

Death toll confirmed at 7, with 23 injured. Live coverage on all national channels and international wire services. The Prime Minister has been briefed. Social media has named the concession company and is publishing the maintenance contract records found online.

PDRM has opened a criminal negligence investigation. Your CEO, Chief Engineer, and Head of Compliance are formally named as persons of interest. All structural inspection and maintenance records for the collapsed section and every other flyover on your network are immediately subpoenaed.

The Minister of Works has announced an immediate safety audit of ALL elevated structures on ALL concession highways nationwide. SPAN and JKR have issued a stop-work order on your entire network pending structural clearance. All remaining flyovers and bridges on your highway are closed as a precaution.

Families of the deceased are holding a press conference with their lawyers. Seven civil suits filed. A criminal charge under Section 304A of the Penal Code (causing death by negligence) is being prepared. Your insurer has issued a reservation of rights letter — coverage is not confirmed.

Parliamentary emergency session. The concession agreement is under government review — termination clause is being assessed. Your company's credit rating has been downgraded by two notches. Three institutional shareholders have divested. The structural investigation report will take 6 months.

Structural clearance received for 80% of remaining flyovers — partial reopening permitted. Preliminary investigation finding leaked to media: fatigue cracking in the collapsed section's expansion joints was flagged in an internal inspection 14 months ago. The report was not acted upon.

Government announces a Special Committee to review all highway concession agreements. Full structural investigation report released: the collapse was caused by long-term deferred maintenance. Criminal charges formally filed against two senior engineers. Concession renewal application placed on hold indefinitely.

recovery_levers.label: Declare Mass Casualty Incident — Full Emergency Protocol
recovery_levers.description: Immediately declare a mass casualty incident and activate your full emergency response protocol. Assign a single incident commander. Establish a command post adjacent to (not on) the collapse site. Full cooperation with BOMBA search and rescue — provide site drawings and utilities maps immediately.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Incident command is disorganised — emergency services lack site drawings and utilities maps. Response is delayed.

recovery_levers.label: CEO Issues Immediate Personal Statement
recovery_levers.description: CEO appears on camera within 90 minutes — not a press release, not a spokesperson. Personal acknowledgement of the tragedy. No deflection. Express condolences unreservedly. Confirm full cooperation with all investigations. This is the only communication posture that limits reputational catastrophe at this scale.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: CEO is unreachable or sends a written statement — perceived as hiding. Media and public response is severe.

recovery_levers.label: Legal Counsel and Crisis Management Firm — Immediate Engagement
recovery_levers.description: Engage criminal defence and civil liability legal counsel and a major crisis management firm within 2 hours. Instruct all employees: do not speak to media, investigators, or external parties without legal counsel present.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Employees make unguided statements to investigators. Legal exposure compounds. Evidence chain mismanaged.

recovery_levers.label: Proactive Structural Safety Audit — Entire Network
recovery_levers.description: Do not wait for the Minister's announcement. Commission an independent structural audit of every flyover and bridge on your network and announce it publicly before the Ministry orders one. This single act partially reclaims the safety narrative.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Ministry orders the audit first — you are reactive, not proactive. Narrative control is lost entirely.

recovery_levers.label: Victim Family Support Programme
recovery_levers.description: Establish a dedicated family liaison team with HR and external welfare specialists. Contact next-of-kin directly and personally before the press conference. Offer immediate financial assistance without waiting for legal processes. This is both ethically correct and legally strategic.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Families hear of support options only from lawyers — legal costs and hostility escalate significantly.

recovery_levers.label: Locate and Secure All Maintenance and Inspection Records
recovery_levers.description: Within 2 hours: locate, secure, and legally preserve every inspection report, maintenance log, and work order for the collapsed section and all similar structures. Do this before subpoenas arrive. If there are gaps or concerning findings, brief legal counsel immediately — do not destroy or conceal anything.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Records are located and handed to investigators in a disorganised state — or worse, are found to be missing. Criminal exposure multiplies.

recovery_levers.label: Engage Government Relations and Concession Authority
recovery_levers.description: Senior leadership meets with the concession authority and Ministry within 24 hours — not to defend, but to present a full accountability and remediation roadmap. Demonstrate that the company is an active partner in resolution, not a defendant in hiding.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Government proceeds with concession review without any direct engagement from the company — termination risk increases.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lessons: (1) This is a maximum severity scenario — no team will achieve a high score. The learning is in the decision-making under existential pressure, not in 'winning'. (2) The leaked internal inspection report in Month 2 (Wave 7) is the scenario's most important teaching moment — it demonstrates that a BCM plan cannot substitute for actual maintenance compliance. If you deferred maintenance and it caused the event, no amount of crisis response can fully recover your position. (3) Teams consistently underestimate the concession termination risk — they focus on reconstruction and neglect the government relationship levers. (4) The CEO personal statement lever (LOG04-L2) should generate significant discussion: most teams want to wait for facts before the CEO speaks. The debrief should challenge this instinct directly. (5) The victim family support lever (LOG04-L5) is ethically non-negotiable — any team that skips it for cost reasons should have this reflected in the debrief conversation. Facilitator note: run a values-based debrief for this scenario, not just a process debrief.

industries.name: Manufacturing & Supply Chain
industries.archetype: Production continuity-driven, supplier-dependent, safety-critical in some sub-sectors

scenarios.name: Key Supplier Sudden Shutdown
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: RM 800K–3M+ in lost production value and contract penalties depending on duration
scenarios.trigger_text: Your sole supplier of a critical sub-component has just announced an immediate shutdown due to a labour dispute at their facility. No timeline for resolution. You have exactly 4 days of raw material inventory remaining on the production floor.
scenarios.threat_summary: Single-source supplier failure causing production shutdown — no alternate supplier qualified, customer orders at risk.

escalation_waves.event: Supply Chain team is calling every potential alternate supplier. None are immediately qualified. Production continues on reserves — 4 days left.
Production rate reduced to 60% capacity. Major customer orders are at risk of missing delivery dates. Account managers are starting to receive calls.
Financial impact assessed: RM 1.1M in unfulfilled orders by end of this week alone. Finance is revising the monthly forecast downward.
Production halts on two lines. Raw material inventory exhausted. 120 production workers have no assigned tasks.
A major customer cancels a RM 3.2M contract and sources from a competitor. Word is spreading in the industry about your supply reliability.
A new alternate supplier has been identified but requires a full 3-week qualification process before any material can be used in production.

recovery_levers.label: Emergency Dual-Sourcing Protocol
recovery_levers.description: Activate emergency supplier search across your network and industry contacts. Engage a procurement specialist to fast-track identification.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No one is authorised or resourced to run an emergency supplier search.

recovery_levers.label: Prioritise Remaining Stock
recovery_levers.description: Immediately triage remaining inventory — allocate to highest-margin and most contractually-critical orders only. Freeze lower-priority production.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Stock allocated on first-come-first-served basis — highest-value orders not protected.

recovery_levers.label: Proactive Customer Communication
recovery_levers.description: Contact at-risk customers before they call you. Be honest about the timeline. Offer partial delivery or revised schedules. Protect the relationship.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Customers discover the delay when their delivery fails to arrive — trust damage is significantly worse.

recovery_levers.label: Bridge Supply Negotiation
recovery_levers.description: Negotiate a short-term component supply bridge with a competitor manufacturer or through a distributor. Higher cost but maintains production.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No budget authority to negotiate premium emergency supply terms without Finance sign-off.

recovery_levers.label: Fast-Track Supplier Qualification
recovery_levers.description: Dedicate Quality and Procurement teams full-time to compress the 3-week qualification process. Accept higher initial QA costs to move faster.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Qualification timeline cannot be compressed — 3 weeks becomes 6 weeks.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lesson: Single-source supplier dependency is the central lesson. Teams learn it the hard way when they realise no alternate lever works without a qualified supplier. The customer communication lever is consistently activated too late — after the customer has already called. The stock prioritisation decision (who gets the last components?) often generates the most debate in debrief.

scenarios.name: Factory Fire — Partial Production Facility Loss
scenarios.war_chest_impact_label: RM 8M+ in direct asset loss; RM 500K–1.5M per week in lost production revenue
scenarios.trigger_text: A fire breaks out in the raw materials storage area at 2:00 AM. BOMBA is on site and contains it within 3 hours — but one production hall is completely destroyed. The good news: no fatalities. The bad news: 45% of your production capacity is gone.
scenarios.threat_summary: Fire destroys one production hall — 45% capacity loss, DOSH investigation, insurance claim, and customer supply impact.

escalation_waves.event: Fire is contained. One production hall confirmed destroyed. RM 8M in equipment lost. Night shift staff are accounted for — no injuries.
CEO and senior leadership on site. Insurance claim process initiated. DOSH (occupational safety authority) has been notified and is sending an inspector.
Key customers notified of supply delays. Legal team reviewing force majeure clauses. Two customers are indicating they may invoke contract penalties.
Insurance assessor on site. Preliminary estimate: 3–6 weeks for partial restoration. Production workers on two lines have no work assignment.
DOSH investigation identifies a maintenance log gap from 6 months ago. Potential compliance violation. Fine and stop-work order possible.
An alternate production site has been shortlisted but requires a 2-week setup. A competitor approaches two of your major customers with a supply offer.

recovery_levers.label: Trigger Insurance Claim Immediately
recovery_levers.description: Initiate business interruption insurance claim on Day 1. Document all damage photographically before any clean-up begins. Brief your insurance broker.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Claim filed late or incompletely — insurance payout delayed or reduced.

recovery_levers.label: Activate Alternate Site Protocol
recovery_levers.description: Identify and contract a third-party manufacturer or activate a secondary facility for partial production continuity while main site recovers.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: No alternate site can be contracted without Production team to specify requirements.

recovery_levers.label: Proactive Customer Communication
recovery_levers.description: Contact all affected customers within 24 hours with a realistic recovery timeline. Honesty protects the relationship; silence invites contract penalties.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Customers informed only when delivery fails — relationship damage significantly greater.

recovery_levers.label: DOSH Proactive Engagement
recovery_levers.description: Prepare a preliminary safety incident report and submit to DOSH proactively — before the inspector arrives. Demonstrate compliance commitment.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: DOSH inspector arrives to a company with no prepared documentation — worst possible impression.

recovery_levers.label: Employee Welfare & Trauma Support
recovery_levers.description: Activate employee assistance programme for night shift staff and workers from the affected hall. Communicate clearly about pay continuity during downtime.
recovery_levers.if_department_missing: Staff are left without support or clear communication — morale deteriorates, informal social media posts appear.

scenarios.debrief_notes: Key lesson: Insurance documentation must happen before clean-up, which feels counterintuitive under pressure. Teams frequently deploy Operations to clean up immediately, inadvertently destroying the evidence trail needed for the claim. The DOSH maintenance log wave is a surprise — it teaches teams that BCM also means keeping compliance records current, not just having a recovery plan.

BIA_Manufacturing.document_title: Business Impact Analysis — Manufacturing & Supply Chain
